title: Minimum Wage Australia Casual: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary
description: Understand the minimum wage australia casual rate, calculate annual salary from hourly pay, and compare award wages. Includes tax and super estimates for 2026-27.
salarySummary: Based on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, the annual gross pay is approximately $52,263 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage australia casual rate?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage for casual employees is $33.05 per hour, which includes the 25% casual loading on the base rate of $26.44. However, many awards set higher rates depending on the industry and classification.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52. The calculator on this site does that for you, and also shows fortnightly, weekly, tax, and super estimates.

faqs.q: Does the calculator include super and tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay. Tax uses the 2026-27 resident rates with the full tax-free threshold and Medicare levy. It is an estimate only, not a determination of your actual pay or tax.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Minimum Wage Australia Casual Rate

The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum pay rate for most employees in Australia. From 1 July 2026, the Fair Work Commission set it at $26.44 per hour for permanent employees. For casual workers, a 25% loading is added, making the **minimum wage australia casual** rate $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for entitlements casuals do not receive, such as paid leave.

However, many workers are covered by an award or registered agreement that sets a higher rate than the National Minimum Wage. Always check your award or agreement first. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has more details on current rates.

### How to Calculate Annual Salary from Hourly Pay

The standard formula to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary is:

**hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a full-time week of 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. For example:

- Permanent minimum wage: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,263 per year (gross)
- Casual minimum wage: $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,329 per year (gross)

If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide explains this in more detail.

### Fortnightly Pay

Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. Using the minimum wage examples:

- Permanent: $1,004.90 per week → $2,009.80 per fortnight
- Casual: $1,256.10 per week → $2,512.20 per fortnight

Knowing your fortnightly amount is useful for budgeting and comparing salary offers.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the floor. Many industries have modern awards that set higher minimum rates for specific roles. For instance, hospitality, retail, and construction awards often exceed the national minimum. Casual loading of 25% applies on top of the base award rate, not on top of penalty rates or allowances.

If you are covered by an award, your minimum hourly rate (including casual loading if applicable) will be higher than $26.44. Use the [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data) to find your correct classification.

### Casual Loading Explained

Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate. It is intended to compensate for the lack of paid sick leave, annual leave, and other benefits that permanent employees receive. When using our [timesheet](/), enter your base hourly rate (without loading) and check the casual loading box. **Do not** enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

## Tax and Super Estimates

Once you have your annual gross pay, you can estimate tax and super.

### Superannuation Guarantee

Employers must pay super at 12% of your ordinary earnings on top of your gross salary. For the National Minimum Wage:

- Permanent: $52,263 × 12% = $6,271.56 per year
- Casual: $65,329 × 12% = $7,839.48 per year

Super is paid on top, not deducted from your pay. It stops once your earnings exceed the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026-27). See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

### Income Tax (2026-27 Resident Rates)

Using the tax-free threshold of $18,200 and the progressive rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- Over $190,000: $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

Plus Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income (with possible reductions for low incomes). For a permanent minimum wage earner ($52,263), the estimated tax (including Medicare) is roughly $6,647. Your actual tax may differ based on deductions and other factors. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised estimate.

## Average Weekly Earnings Reference

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) for May 2026 show:

- Full-time adult ordinary time earnings: $2,083.70 per week
- All employees total earnings (including part-time): $1,579.20 per week

These are **averages**, not medians for any specific job or industry. They include all full-time adults across Australia. Do not use them as a median for your occupation. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page has more context.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate. If you are a casual employee, check the casual loading box to add 25% on top. The calculator then shows:

- Annual gross pay (hourly × 38 × 52)
- Weekly and fortnightly gross
- Estimated tax (using 2026-27 rates and Medicare)
- Estimated super (12% of ordinary earnings)

Remember: the calculator assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Important Distinctions

- **National Minimum Wage**: $26.44/hour permanent, $33.05/hour casual (including loading).
- **Award rates**: Higher minimums set by industry; check your award.
- **Casual loading**: 25% on base rate, not on penalties.
- **Super**: 12% paid on top by employer, up to the contribution base.
- **Tax**: Based on total taxable income; use the resident tax scale.

For more details, explore the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) and [job pay](/topics/job-pay) pages.

## Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
